Max Havelaar is a novel published in 1860 by Multatuli, the pen name of Eduard Douwes Dekker, a former Dutch official in Lebak, west Java. It attacked the abuses of Dutch rule in the East Indies.

It tells how Javanese peasants were squeezed by local chiefs and Dutch officials under the Cultivation System, which forced them to grow export crops such as coffee. The book shocked readers in the Netherlands.

It helped bring the end of the system and the later Ethical Policy of schools and irrigation. Pramoedya Ananta Toer called it the book that killed colonialism. See coffee in Java.
